records.detail: Amundi Asset Management is one of three outside firms the Banco Central de Bolivia hires to invest the Fondo RAL-ME, the foreign-currency reserve requirement that Bolivian banks must hold at the central bank. The central bank says it manages this fund the same way it manages the international reserves. The fund held USD 1,052 million on 31 December 2018. The report also records two breaches by Amundi in 2018: on 23 January and 22 October it traded through Wells Fargo Securities International Limited, a broker not approved for the fund, and on 30 November it went over the 5 percent limit on exposure to a single bank, a position sold on 3 December 2018.

leads_not_opened.lead: Central Bank of Lesotho Annual Report 2024 (https://centralbank.org.ls/wp-content/uploads/2024-Central-Bank-of-Lesotho-Annual-Report-4.pdf, 60 MB, read). The narrative 'RESERVES MANAGEMENT' section names no manager - it covers only the Act of 2000 objectives, governance and 2024 returns. But the credit-risk note's counterparty exposure tables carry the row labels 'Bank of N.Y (RAMP)', 'Crown Agents' (both GBP and USD lines), 'World Bank RAMP', 'United States-RAMP' and 'RAMP T Bills'. Those labels show Lesotho runs a RAMP portfolio and has exposure to Crown Agents, but no sentence in the report says either body manages a portfolio, so under the no-upgrade rule nothing was filed. A hand check of the full financial-statements notes, or of the Bank's reserves-management page https://centralbank.org.ls/index.php/financial-markets-about/598-reserves-management, should settle whether Crown Agents Investment Management and the World Bank hold mandates. Crown Agents Investment Management is confirmed as a reserves manager for Seychelles in this round, which raises the odds.

Earlier editions on nationalassembly.sc were not searched; the CAIM USD portfolio runs from 2014 and the CNY portfolio from 2022, so earlier editions would date the start of each mandate. The report also mentions SADC and RAMP workshops and a CAIM central banking course - training, not management, so nothing was filed from those.

leads_not_opened.country: Method note for the next round
leads_not_opened.lead: Two document types carried this round and should be tried first next time. (1) A standalone reserves-management report tabled in a national parliament, not on the central bank's own site: Seychelles' came from nationalassembly.sc and Fiji's annual report from parliament.gov.fj. Parliamentary hosts do not block automated retrieval the way central bank sites increasingly do - nbp.pl, nbrm.mk, bcrp.gob.pe, bcp.gov.py, bom.mu and portalunico.iaip.gob.hn all refused or broke this round. Searching 'site:parliament.* central bank annual report reserves' style queries for the remaining Commonwealth and Pacific countries is likely to pay. (2) The accounting-policy note on financial assets designated at fair value through profit or loss. In Tanzania's statements the sentence that gave the whole answer - 'These are foreign currency marketable securities that are externally managed' - sits in the Note 3 accounting policies, about 2,000 lines before the reserves note itself. Grep the policy note for 'externally managed', not just the reserves note. Also note that bom.mu fails TLS verification through the proxy for curl but is reachable with the fetch tool, so a TLS error on a central bank host is worth one retry with the other tool.
